candidate: decode attention pass 3: register-prefetched V loads (depth 4) plus geometry-selected two-dimension loads
reason: bit-exact against the block kernel and cuts the pass that the iteration-22 ablation identified as 57-71% of the decode attention kernel: sliding 427.9 -> 318.9 us and full 696.0 -> 339.8 us at keys=1024, full 1174 -> 509.5 us at keys=2048. Campaign metric 33.0213 -> 41.9049 tok/s (+26.9%), +160% over the 16.0931 baseline

mechanism.diagnosis: iteration 22 closed with a timing-only ablation that removed pass 3's V loads: sliding 427.9 -> 183.4 us, full 696.0 -> 204.1 us. Pass 3 was moving 16.78 MB unique at full in 492 us (34 GB/s) while the same loop without the loads moved 100.66 MB issued in 204 us (493 GB/s), so it was latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound
mechanism.cause: each lane walks all `keys` with one 2-byte load per key inside a dependent accumulate chain, and the `weight == 0` skip that the block kernel uses stops the compiler from hoisting those loads, so the walk serialised at memory latency: ~1024 loads per lane at ~240-480 ns matches the measured 244-492 us
mechanism.fix: load the V value of key j + kPrefetch into a register while key j is accumulated, so the loads have independent addresses that issue ahead of use. The pipeline only changes *when* a load is issued: the accumulation stays the ascending-j chain per dimension and the `weight == 0` skip is untouched, so the result is unchanged bit for bit
mechanism.second_fix: when head_dim >= 2 * threads (the full-attention geometry, head_dim 512 with 256 threads) lane L owns the dimensions 2L and 2L+1 and issues one gemma4_pair2 load - 4 bytes for 16-bit KV, 8 for 32-bit - instead of two 2-byte loads. The alignas on the pair type is what makes the compiler emit a single vector load; it holds because head_dim is even for every geometry the launcher routes here and the KV base is a device allocation. The sliding geometry (head_dim 256 = threads) keeps the scalar load, since a two-dimension mapping there would idle half the block: measured 336.9 us two-wide against 318.9 us scalar
mechanism.pipeline_depth: kPrefetch swept at 2/4/8/16: 384.1/315.7/336.0/337.6 us sliding and 578.1/419.3/464.4/465.3 us full. Depth 4 is the optimum on both geometries; deeper pipelines lose to register pressure

correctness.contract: bit-exact with the block kernel (same-schedule arithmetic): only *when* a load is issued and which lane owns which dimension changed, never the per-dimension ascending-j accumulation order or the weight==0 skip
correctness.parity_result: green together with tests/test_gpu_gemma4_attention_geometry.py - bitwise equality on every shape, both dtypes, keep and holes masks, including the two-dimension load path (head_dim 512) and the scalar path (head_dim 256) at keys 1..8192
